clue.text: There is something insignificant in the splashdown

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount set against a vast whole, the idiom for a trifling contribution
a spacecraft's splashdown is literally a fall of a capsule into the sea

explanation.surface: A remark that a space capsule's landing at sea has some trivial detail in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a contribution too small to matter; read literally it describes something falling into the sea, as a capsule does at splashdown.

clue.text: Forcible doctor finds a good man in charge

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword's good man

explanation.surface: A forceful physician turns out to be a decent person in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are severe and vigorous ones, forceful in their effect.

clue.text: Improving like a seamstress

definitions.meaning: getting better after an illness or setback
read literally, a seamstress is busy at her repairs, occupied with mending clothes

explanation.surface: A patient recovering is compared with someone doing needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for recovering health, and literally pictures someone working on darning and patching.

clue.text: Flew ton high and finished in the sea

definitions.text: Flew ton high and finished in the sea

parts.words: Flew ton high and finished in the sea
parts.note: the myth of the boy with wax wings who went near the sun, whose wax melted so he dropped into the Aegean

explanation.surface: An overambitious flyer ends up in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Daedalus's son soared toward the sun on wax wings, which melted, and he drowned in the sea named after him.

clue.text: See 1
Chief geographical feature of Flamborough

definitions.meaning: the leader or person in charge
a headland; Flamborough's chalk promontory juts into the North Sea on the Yorkshire coast

explanation.surface: The main landmark on a stretch of the Yorkshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief is the leader of a group, and a promontory is called by the same word, as at Flamborough in Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: Presumably guarantees deep sleep

parts.note: a mattress for slumber is imagined at the bottom of the sea, where depth is literal

explanation.surface: A claim about a mattress that promises sound slumber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep sleep' means sound sleep in the surface, but a sea floor is a resting place at great depth.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea floor is jokily treated as a place to lie down, where any sleep would certainly be deep.

clue.text: Stands upright before the court

parts.note: ERE is an old word meaning before
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone rises to their feet in front of the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stands' is a link word here, joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect describes something held straight and vertical, not bent or slumped.

clue.text: Incomplete -and socially unacceptable

definitions.meaning: a task left unfinished has not yet been carried out
behaviour frowned on by polite society, against etiquette

explanation.surface: Something both unfinished and bad form.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfinished work is literally not completed, and the same phrase is an idiom for a breach of good manners.

clue.text: Always includes an odd star in a lost state

indicators.note: the word for always surrounds the rearranged letters, so it takes them inside

parts.note: AY, or aye, is an old word for always

indicators.note: an odd star is a peculiar one, so the letters of star are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: A peculiar star keeps appearing, always in a confusing place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges STAR into STRA, which 'includes' puts inside AY.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray means wandering off course, ending up lost.

clue.text: Window designed, we hear, to follow suit

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first, following on behind it

parts.note: a lawsuit is a legal case

indicators.note: the sound of the spoken word is used, not its spelling, as listeners pick it up

parts.note: something designed for a purpose was meant for it

explanation.surface: A window intended to match the others in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like matching cards or style, but it is a legal action, CASE; 'we hear' turns MEANT into MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a hinged window that opens outward like a door.

clue.text: Measuring instruments in elude nothing for short-lived luminaries

indicators.note: the instruments take the zero inside their letters, holding it within

parts.note: meters are devices for gauging quantities like gas or electricity
O, shaped like a zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Gauges register nothing during a brief celestial display.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting stars blaze briefly across the night sky, bright lights that last only seconds.

clue.text: Nine with the Customs after them

indicators.note: the word for customs is placed behind the other piece, coming after it

parts.note: customs are habits or usages, so uses

explanation.surface: Nine people have the Customs officers chasing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' suggests the border service, but it means habitual practices, USES.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine goddesses of Greek myth presiding over arts and sciences are numbered at nine.

clue.text: "____ ____ and through and through the vorpal blade went snicker-snack" (Carroll)

definitions.text: "____ ____ and through and through the vorpal blade went snicker-snack" (Carroll)

parts.words: "____ ____ and through and through the vorpal blade went snicker-snack" (Carroll)
parts.note: a line from Lewis Carroll's poem Jabberwocky, with its opening counting words left blank

explanation.surface: A gap-fill quotation from Carroll's nonsense poem about slaying a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The full line of Jabberwocky opens with a count of the first two numbers, the rhythm of the sword strokes.

clue.text: Dally i.e. to change the perfect solution

definitions.note: an adverb meaning in the best possible case, glossed by a noun phrase

indicators.note: the letters given are made to change position into a new word

explanation.surface: Advice to stop dawdling, since dallying must change to reach the right answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally describes how things would go in a perfect world, the best possible outcome.

clue.text: The gang boasted

definitions.meaning: a team of workers or a group of people acting together
an old past tense of crow, to brag

explanation.surface: The gang bragged.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a team or group, and as a past tense of crow it means bragged, crowed.

clue.text: Housewife essential to anyone who is 2

definitions.text: Housewife essential to anyone who is 2

parts.words: Housewife essential to anyone who is 2
parts.note: a housewife or hussif is a small sewing kit, vital to anyone like a seamstress at her darning

explanation.surface: A homemaker's must-have for someone recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is ON THE MEND, read as busy mending. 'Housewife' looks like a person but is an old name for a pocket sewing kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder for sewing pins and thread, a housewife kit, is what anyone mending clothes needs.

clue.text: It goes up to the course In any aversion

indicators.note: the reversed word and the route are placed inside the letters of any
in a down entry, a word that rises is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a path is a course or route

explanation.surface: Something climbs toward the racecourse with distaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns IT into TI; then TIPATH goes 'In' ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipathy is a strong dislike, a feeling of hostility towards something.

clue.text: Evergreen remark of Hero to her lover

parts.note: O is an exclamation, a cry of address
in Greek legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit Hero, his beloved

explanation.surface: A tree is what a Greek heroine called out to her man.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero here is the legendary priestess; her cry 'O Leander!' gives the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is an evergreen Mediterranean shrub with leathery leaves that stay green all year.

clue.text: Conservative course does this also lead to Scotland?

definitions.meaning: a moderate path avoiding extremes

definitions.text: does this also lead to Scotland?
definitions.meaning: pictures a central highway heading north, as if a route up the middle of Britain

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the moderate political way is also the way north.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the moderate line is the idiom of a middle way, which literally sounds like a central road running north.

clue.text: A cry of disappointment rises to spoil the wine

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that rises reads upward, so its letters are backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow

explanation.surface: A disappointed groan goes up at ruining the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns ALAS into SALA, which follows MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily.

clue.text: Philosophical porch

parts.note: the painted colonnade in Athens where Zeno taught, giving the Stoic school its name

explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a Greek covered colonnade; the Stoics took their name from the one in Athens where Zeno taught.

clue.text: Hold off the sailor on the spot

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sits on top of the other, coming first

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: Keeping the seaman away while he stands right there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the spot' looks like 'immediately', but 'spot' is a mark, STAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain or hold back from doing something.

clue.text: " My life is-like a — - upon the beach" (Thoreau)

definitions.text: " My life is-like a — - upon the beach" (Thoreau)

parts.words: " My life is-like a — - upon the beach" (Thoreau)
parts.note: a line from Henry David Thoreau's writing comparing life to a leisurely walk by the shore

explanation.surface: A gap-fill quotation in which Thoreau likens life to an amble on the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoreau wrote that his life was like a leisurely walk on the beach, a gentle amble.

clue.text: Bird for a policeman

definitions.meaning: a name for the goldfinch, from its red face
slang for a military police officer

explanation.surface: A bird stands in for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldfinch has been called this from its red head, and British military police wear scarlet caps, giving them the nickname.

clue.text: Curtails the weeds

definitions.meaning: cuts short, as a tail or pay is cut
broad-leaved plants of the sorrel family growing as weeds

explanation.surface: Someone cuts back the weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock is to cut short or reduce, and dock is also a common broad-leaved weed.

clue.text: Alias the Ornithorhynchus

parts.note: the scientific genus name of the duck-billed egg-laying mammal from Australia, given as another name

explanation.definitionFit: Ornithorhynchus is the genus of the duck-billed Australian monotreme, whose common name this is.

clue.text: Season for a trip

definitions.meaning: the American name for autumn
a stumble or tumble

explanation.surface: A time of year for a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call autumn by this name, and to trip is to stumble and go down.

clue.text: Simple oriental magistrate in an island

indicators.note: the magistrate is placed inside the island's letters

parts.note: Aran is an island off Ireland
a cadi is a judge in Muslim countries

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated Eastern judge lives on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: CADI, a Muslim judge, is a word mainly met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadian describes the simple rustic life of idealised Arcadia.

clue.text: Left with a first class return from The Merchant

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: the first-class term comes back, read in the other direction

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A trader departs, coming back first-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns AI (A1) into IA. 'The Merchant' is Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, who disguises herself as a lawyer.

clue.text: Competently includes the irrational in ridiculous manner

indicators.note: the adverb for skilfully holds the irrational number within its letters

parts.note: ably means skilfully or competently
a surd is an irrational number, such as a root that cannot be written exactly

explanation.surface: A skilled performer brings in irrational ideas, to silly effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irrational' looks like unreasonable, but it is a mathematical surd, an irrational root.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurdly means in a ludicrous or nonsensical way.

clue.text: To continue the same means' dismissal for the batsman

definitions.meaning: to carry on playing as before
in cricket, a batsman is out when the ball deflects off the bat onto the stumps, described as played on

explanation.surface: Explaining a cricket term for carrying on.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going is to carry on playing; in cricket, being out by edging the ball onto your own stumps is described with the same words.
